page.layout: One column of running text; left margin holds two notes beside the last paragraph (the marginal note aligned with "In factis" and its continuation). Page number and running head at the top; catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: VIII. Quid enim? an quibus sociennus iste tuus parentibus sit ortus ignoras: aut illud nescis, ex illius maioribus neminem nisi improbitate ac sceleribus notum fuisse.
IX. Hinc, ut proverbio dicitur, [illegible, ~20 letters]: parentis mali pessimus filius, qui a pueris nihil boni domi vidit, audiuit, didicit.

X. Praeceptores quidem habuit optimos: sed eos nasofusspendit adunco: disciplinam ferre non potuit: in cauponulis saepius, quo vel templis, vel scholis conspici sese passus est: aes alienum grande, infciis parentibus contraxit: in concubia usque noctem potauit: amoribus operam dedit turpibus: quid dicam amplius? ex omnibus vitiis quasi compositus et conflatus est.
XI. Itaque quis te malus genius ad illius amicitiam atq; familiaritatem pertraxerit ignoro: sed doleo interim vehementer.

XII. Seuere etiam tibi mando: ut in posterum ab illius conuersatione abstineas, eaq; in re, et mandati diuini, et Academiae, in qua vivis, et mei, qui, ut nosti, profectionis istius author tibi extiti, et deniq; tuae famae atq; existimationis rationem habeas.
XIII. Sin minus, in grauem, nō meam solum, verum etiam mecaenatū tuorū, atq; adeo bonorum omnium offensione incurres: poenas quoq; eas expectabis, quas non obedientibus minari Dominum nostri.
In factis vituperandis caufe, effecta, adiuncta & comparata potissimum valent. SoActionis & factorum vitae operationes. [?]

page.notes: The Greek in paragraph IX is not legible enough to transcribe letter by letter; it is marked illegible. The left margin note is partly worn; its reading "Actionis & factorum vitae operationes" is doubtful. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout. The initial word "sociennus" is doubtful (the first letter may be f or s). The word "concubia" is printed as "concubiã" with a tilde for n, read as concubiā. The catchword "let" sits at the lower right.
